cars.specification_market: Original 1970s Ligier JS2 production-road GT family, selected early French 2.7-litre brochure specification with 1972 reference year. Four-page Automobiles Ligier brochure is undated in its printed text: host filename calls it 1971 and cover bears a 1972 annotation; no exact publication or launch date inferred. Manufacturer history places the effective production debut in 1972. Group 2.7/3.0/Merak SS road engines, body updates, years, equipment and chassis once. JS1/JS3 prototypes, racing JS2s and the 2018 JS2 R are not selected or additionally counted. All 23 technical attributes map to this early road brochure. Preserve its 2670 cc and 170 CV DIN at 5500 rpm rather than substituting other catalogues' displacement or later output. No exact engine-code suffix, carburettor brand, chassis metal skin, weight basis, maximum speed, measured acceleration, production total, later 195/220-hp or competition 270/330-hp/DFV figures are imported.
cars.summary: The original Ligier JS2 embodied Guy Ligier and Michel Têtu's French mid-engine GT project, combining a Maserati-powered road coupe with practical cabin and luggage packaging. Its engineering and competition lineage, including the racing programme's 1974 Tour de France Automobile victory, give it a lasting place in French sports-car history. Count the original road family once; rarity alone and racing specifications are not the basis for adding extra versions.

sources.notes: Downloaded four-page image-only PDF; all four pages individually rendered and inspected. Cover JS2/Ligier and back-cover Automobiles Ligier Abrest-Vichy imprint establish manufacturer origin. Filename says 1971, cover annotation 1972, printed publication date not established. All 23 attributes map to technical panel index 2; dimensions convert stated metres to mm. It explicitly describes a two-seat mid-engine grand routiere derived from JS1, not a competition-only JS1. Retain 2670 cc/170 CV DIN/23.5 mkg labels. No carburettor brand, exact engine-code suffix, inferred chassis-metal skin, 850-kg weight basis, claimed maximum speed or later/racing values imported.

sources.title: The Ligier JS2s starred in the 1973 and 1974 Tour de France automobile — 4 May 2022
sources.source_type: Original manufacturer programme history with engineer testimony
sources.notes: Complete relevant article body read. Places true debut in 1972, explains insufficient road production for GT-class homologation and distinguishes the resulting prototype-class race programme. Supports 1974 Tour de France racing one-two after substantial aerodynamic/mechanical development, not a stock road result. Earlier failures and sales limitations retained. Article contains inconsistent race-number details; none imported. No 1973 stage totals, 1975 chassis number, general engine-production chronology, race tuning or modern JS2 R specification transferred to the selected road car.

sources.publisher: Classic Courses; Olivier Rogar interviewing Michel Têtu
sources.title: Michel Têtu 1/2 — Les inédits de Pilote et Gentleman, 1 January 2022, Ligier section
sources.source_type: Original interview with the car's engineering designer
sources.notes: Introduction and complete relevant Ligier interview section read; not an audit of the entire career article or second instalment. Têtu explains JS2 road accommodation, increased wheelbase/interior height and road/race chassis distinction: competition aluminium sandwich skins replaced production steel. No inferred chassis metal is added to the selected brochure's generic sandwich description. Gearbox development chronology is contextual and supplies no selected ratio or year-specific specification. JS1/JS3 and racing engine/chassis details remain separate.

sources.title: Guy Ligier's legacy lives on with the Maserati-powered JS2
sources.source_type: Original retrospective road-car visit and historical feature
sources.notes: Complete relevant feature body read, including original visit to a final-iteration 1975 road example. Supports French GT heritage, practical packaging and racing context; not a contemporary test or numerical authority for the early brochure. Production totals explicitly vary, so none imported. Race engine problems and later DFV Le Mans result do not describe standard road reliability or engine. Retrofitted Maserati badge, dealer equipment and later body/wheels do not establish original early specification. No sale price or investment recommendation imported.

facts.title: A racing one-two explains the road family's heritage
facts.explanation: After major racing development, Ligier JS2s finished first and second in the 1974 Tour de France Automobile. This belongs to the competition programme and explains the production GT's heritage; it is not a claim that the early 2.7-litre road car used the winning racers' engine, lightweight chassis or aerodynamics.
